name: Ferry Pole Primer (Sanh Độ Quyết)
concept: The ferry children's method, learned standing on a moving deck with a bamboo pole. The pole goes down into the river and Water qi comes up it; the bamboo itself gives a little Wood. At the sixth layer a ferryman can hold a loaded boat still against the spring current. Ashore it gives a steady body and good balance and not much more.
lore: The boat families of the Nine-Bend River taught it to their children long before they banded together as a sect in 790 (A075).

name: Washing Waves Canon (Lãng Đào Kinh)
concept: Named for the gold-washers' saying that after a thousand washings the river sand gives up its gold (A076). The cultivator washes her own qi a thousand times through the meridians in a slow wave, and each layer leaves a little gold behind. In a fight the waves wash a foe's wards away one layer at a time, and what is left of the holder's qi at the end strikes clean through.
lore: The founder Uông Liên Chu put it together from the boat families' songs and the gold-washers' rhythm after the feuds of 786-788 (V047, V048), so that the families would cultivate one method instead of feuding over landings.

name: Nine Bends Art (Cửu Khúc Quyết)
concept: The art of going round. A river does not break a rock; it bends nine times and arrives anyway. The holder slips each blow in a long curve, and every blow she slips builds a Bend; at nine Bends she arrives with the whole river at her back. Swallow Stance is listed in depth prose but omitted from abilities so Water-Wood holders pass CongPhap.usable; Ninth Bend supplies the curving evade step directly.
lore: Giang Cửu Khúc, whose name is the river's nine bends, holds it to the ninth layer. He says he has never once arrived late.
